reasons: Run by the frontend lint command in the quality gate.

terms.meaning: a tool that checks code for mistakes and style problems using rules
the add-on that lets ESLint understand TypeScript code
a rule that uses the type information from TypeScript to check the code
a lint message that does not stop the program but is treated as a failure in this project

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Loading the rule packages
sections.what: Loads the base JavaScript rule set and the TypeScript rule package.
sections.why: Both are needed for the lint checks to run on TypeScript files.
sections.watch_out: The package versions must match those in frontend/package.json or rule names may not match.

sections.name: default export
sections.title: Lint rules and skipped folders
sections.what: Defines the folders to skip, such as build output and coverage reports, applies the base and strict rule sets, and turns off two TypeScript rules.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for turning off the two rules.
sections.watch_out: Turning off rules reduces what lint can catch, so each switched-off rule is a known gap.

summary: Sets the code-quality rules used when the frontend is linted, using strict TypeScript rules and skipping build output.
purpose: Makes the lint command catch code problems in the frontend before a release.
why: Likely reason: strict rules catch type mistakes early. The reason for turning off the two rules is not stated in the code.
how: It combines the base JavaScript rules with the strict TypeScript rule set, points the type-aware checker at the project settings, and turns off two rules.
inputs: The frontend source files and the TypeScript settings found through the project service.
outputs: Lint results in the terminal. The lint command treats any warning as a failure.
risks: Strict rules can flag many small issues. Turning off two rules hides a few kinds of problems from the lint results.
debug: If lint fails after an update, check whether a rule name changed. If the checker cannot find a project, check the TypeScript settings files.
